_description: Wake yourself (or another agent) every N cycles with tool clock_register.

wake_me._description: Get a message every N cycles in your own queue.

rules._description: When it fires, who can change it, what happens when it cannot send.

wake_me:
# Wake me every N cycles

Call clock_register with op add, a name, every and text; leave out box:
{"op": "add", "name": "check-inbox", "every": 10, "text": "Check data/ for new files."}
Every 10 cycles you get a user message "Check data/ for new files. (clock cycle 30)". Remove it with {"op": "rm", "name": "check-inbox"}; list with {"op": "ls"}.
To wake another agent, give box = its STACK/queue. Shell: aos-clock-register add --every N --box BOX NAME TEXT.
rules:
# Clock letters: rules

- It fires when the cycle number divides by every (10, 20, 30 for every 10), not counted from when you added it.
- Anyone who can write the register can add or remove any entry. Nothing is cleaned up automatically: remove your entry when you no longer need it.
- A letter that cannot be sent is only a warning line from the clock; the clock keeps going.
- While you sleep, letters wait in your queue; you get them all when you wake.
